text:
Liam O'Neill: hi team, first day here on platform, quick Q: following the kube quickstart but when I run `kubectl config get-contexts` I only see an `sso-user` context. I ran `aws sso login` and `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev` but contexts still not showing the `payments` namespace/context I expected. any hints? :wave:

Maya Rivera (eng): welcome Liam! A couple things to check: do you have multiple AWS profiles or multiple kubeconfigs being merged? `KUBECONFIG` env var + `~/.kube/config` merge can hide contexts. `kubectl config view --merge --flatten` shows combined config.

Liam O'Neill: ah I do have a personal `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/personal` set in my zshrc. if I unset KUBECONFIG and run update-kubeconfig again will it add the cluster?

Jorge Alvarez (eng-infra): yeah `aws eks update-kubeconfig` writes to whichever kubeconfig file is active. two safe options: `AWS_PROFILE=redwood aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --alias=redwood-dev` (this appends to ~/.kube/config) or `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood aws eks update-kubeconfig ...` then merge manually. we prefer not touching personal kubeconfig for security.

Liam O'Neill: ran `AWS_PROFILE=redwood aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --alias=redwood-dev` and now I see cluster entry but still no `payments` context. is the context created by infra or do I create it?

Maya Rivera: contexts are just a local named tuple of cluster/user/namespace. infra usually creates a serviceaccount and we give you a RoleBinding. For devs we typically expect you to use your SSO user context and rely on RBAC mapping (IAM->k8s) — we don't create per-user contexts for everyone. which access do you need? read pods in `payments` or admin?

Liam O'Neill: need to list pods and view logs in `payments` for debugging, nothing admin.

Jorge Alvarez: ok, we'll add a RoleBinding that grants your SSO user group `devs` a role with get/list/watch on pods in `payments`. @Asha can you confirm group name in SSO?

Asha Kapoor (people-ops): group is `redwood-devs` for SSO -> k8s mapping.

Jorge Alvarez: thanks. I'll create a RoleBinding in `payments` that binds `Group: redwood-devs` to the `payments-reader` Role. Should be done in ~10-15m.

Infra Bot: deployment note: created RoleBinding `payments-reader-bind-redwood-devs` in namespace `payments` by jorge at 2024-06-15T16:37:00Z (ttl: 168h).

Liam O'Neill: awesome thanks. once that's live, do I need to do anything or will my existing `sso-user` context pick up permission?

Maya Rivera: no action needed on your part. your SSO identity maps to the k8s subject and RBAC will allow the actions. you can verify with: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n payments` and `kubectl get pods -n payments`

Liam O'Neill: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n payments` returns `yes` now, `kubectl get pods -n payments` works too. thanks! one more: what's the recommended way to temporarily assume a serviceaccount if I need a different level of access for testing?

Jorge Alvarez: two options: 1) we can mint a short-lived SA token and give it to you via the team vault (we prefer TTL <= 24h), or 2) we can grant you `impersonate` rights to `system:serviceaccount:payments:debug-sa` so you can `kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:payments:debug-sa ...`. option 2 is cleaner for avoiding token files. you likely won't get impersonate by default. ping infra with the use-case if you need it.

Liam O'Neill: cool. I'll stick with SSO + RoleBinding for daily work and request impersionation when needed. thanks all! :raised_hands:

Maya Rivera: quick note for mac users: if you use osx keychain + aws sso plugin, ensure `credential_process` in `~/.aws/credentials` isn't pointing to an old cached binary or you might see stale tokens.

Asha Kapoor: welcome again Liam, happy to set up a short intro with payments team later today if you want to meet folks.

Liam O'Neill: that'd be great, thanks Asha!
